analysis.title: The dollar's $20 trillion AI problem
key_insights: Foreign investors own more than $20 trillion in US equities. Deutsche Bank estimates roughly 90% of the value of foreign-owned US equities reflects accumulated price appreciation rather than net purchases.
Foreign equity inflows now finance the entire US current account deficit, so the dollar depends increasingly on the equity cycle.

Deutsche Bank warns an AI-driven sell-off could trigger a feedback loop between US equities, currency hedging and the dollar. The risk case is stocks and the dollar falling together, with declining real yields confirming a broader repricing of the AI boom.

StoneX shows the five-session correlation between AI sentiment and the dollar at +0.97, versus +0.31 over 20 sessions. If stocks and the dollar fall together, unhedged foreign investors lose on both the equity and currency sides.
Higher currency hedge ratios among foreign investors could add dollar selling pressure even without equity sales.

DB argues rising AI capex expectations have helped push both equities and real yields higher. A synchronized decline in tech stocks, the dollar and real yields would signal investors discounting a weaker AI investment cycle, turning an equity correction into a macro repricing.
Trade implication: beyond shorting tech, the less obvious trade is to short the dollar. Watch the Nasdaq, DXY and US real yields together.

sector_views.rationale: The note frames an AI-driven tech correction as a risk, with the obvious correction trade being to short tech.

macro_indicators.indicator: AI sentiment vs dollar correlation (5-session, StoneX)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Dollar and AI sentiment are moving almost in lockstep, so an AI sell-off would likely coincide with dollar weakness.

macro_indicators.indicator: AI sentiment vs dollar correlation (20-session, StoneX)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The longer-window correlation is much weaker, so the recent jump is a short-term shift.
A decline alongside tech stocks and the dollar would confirm a repricing of the AI capex cycle.

trade_ideas.description: Short the dollar (DXY) as a US-centric AI equity sell-off hedge, alongside or instead of shorting tech
trade_ideas.rationale: A US-centric equity shock could reverse the traditional stock-dollar relationship and force foreign investors to rethink currency hedges.

risk_factors: AI-driven US equity sell-off feeding into dollar weakness through foreign investor losses and hedging.
Dollar's safe-haven properties are being questioned.
A weaker AI investment cycle repricing real yields, equities and the dollar together.
vol_and_positioning: Foreign investors' unhedged US equity exposure exceeds $20 trillion, so hedge ratio changes could drive dollar flows.
Raising currency hedge ratios on US equity holdings could create dollar selling pressure independent of equity sales.

tension_points.bull_case: For much of the past decade, dollar strength cushioned US equity losses for foreign investors.
tension_points.bear_case: A US-centric shock can flip that relationship so stocks and the dollar fall together, with unhedged foreign investors losing on both sides and hedge ratios rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nasdaq, DXY and US real yields do not all decline together.

theme_stances.key_argument: A US-centric equity shock could reverse the traditional stock-dollar relationship and force foreign investors to rethink currency hedges on an enormous stock of US assets.
theme_stances.evidence: The next AI sell-off could become a dollar sell-off.
